newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil patents protection goes into force.
newsitem.headline: Brazil patents protection goes into force.

text.p: Brazil Thursday brought into force patents and copyright protection, a year after Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed a landmark bill on intellectual property rights.

Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles said the law was "vital for the growth of Brazil" and would not only encourage foreign investment but also persuade Brazilian industry to invest more in research and development.
"Brazil has an enormous potential to develop its own patents," Dornelles told reporters in Brazil's third largest city, Belo Horizonte.

The patents bill, passed by Congress just over a year ago after languishing in limbo for nearly five years due to fierce private sector opposition, covers pharmaceuticals, foodstuffs, chemicals and biologically-altered products.
It also contains a so-called pipeline provision, which extends patent protection to products under development.
Washington and the U.S. pharmaceutical industry had long lobbied Brasilia to introduce copyright laws because of widespread piracy.

Senator Fernando Bezerra, head of the National Industry Confederation and author of the patents bill, said the pharmaceuticals industry had already announced $2.7 billion in planned investment over the next few years because of the law.
Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia, speaking at the same news conference, said the law "brought to Brazil a dimension of modernity".
Dornelles and Lampreia were in Belo Horizonte for ministerial talks on the creation of the Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA).
